groups.rationale: Tests target the deleted general-purpose Facet solver, measure/arrange caches, dirt/invalidation accounting, layout diagnostics or virtual geometry IR. Roblox now owns native GUI layout; these exact internal algorithms no longer exist. Control adaptation/behavior tests remain outside this group.

Tests target deleted Facet blueprint/domain nodes, renderer commits, manual property translation, adapters, host/frame/presenter plumbing and instance parking/recycling implementation. Native Compose/Roblox host is now the implementation; public control/lifetime behavior is separately mapped.

Tests target removed Facet services, error boundaries, owner wrappers, scene/application scaffolding or registry inspection APIs. Compose directly supplies lifetime/reactivity/ownership; native public runtime tests cover Facet integration.

Tests target deleted Facet text metrics, premeasurement/layout approximation and text-fitting solver internals. Native Roblox text measurement/editing is the owner; TextInput UTF8/commit/cancel policy remains under input-family review.

Source-text assertions and fixture artifact identity tied specifically to old blueprint/native adapter/scaffold implementation. Replacement architecture/import/package audits inspect the actual native source.
The intermediate src/native_controls prototype API was deleted. Tests now exercise the completed direct native public library in native_inputs/navigation/collections/themes_media and real examples.

Candidate exact mechanisms: general constraint/layout/text algorithms, removed Facet animation/clock APIs and presentation transforms, private ownership/scheduler/scaffolding APIs, frame/commit accounting. Any surviving control policy must remain under family behavioral mappings.

groupRationales.name: third-reviewed-extraction-and-adapter-mechanisms
groupRationales.rationale: Root approved exact thirdReview case inventory; old renderer extraction seams, adapter/style switches, core harness and schema registration were deleted. Native registration/documentation consistency requires separate native contract checks.

groupRationales.name: removed-layout-solver-policy-and-diagnostic-contracts
groupRationales.rationale: Assertions invoke the deleted Facet solver/environment/blueprint tree, solved rect diagnostics, partial-arrangement counters, waiver sweeps, region negotiation and distance-scale policies. Native Roblox layout and Insets/TextSize replace these mechanisms; this retirement does not claim native pixel geometry equivalence.

reports a src area no row claims
reports a claimed path that does not exist
reports two src paths claimed by the same two areas
reports the two tables falling out of step
reports a spec filed under an area it does not require
reports a spec file that has been renamed away
reports a Studio scenario that is not a registered scenario
reports an empty scenario cell that gives no reason
reports a gate row the manifest does not have
reports a gate stage the manifest does not have
reports a public seam the library has stopped exporting
reports a boundary rule check_boundary does not enforce
reports a link that resolves nowhere
reports a link whose anchor is not a heading in the target
reports a shipped extension playbook the map stops linking
reports a missing marker rather than silently checking nothing
derives a per-area covering count from the require graph

groupRationales.name: removed-text-modifier-facades
groupRationales.rationale: Deleted generic UI.textReveal/UI.valueReveal blueprint modifiers, grapheme-state renderer annotation and delayed overflow disclosure manager. Native TextBox/TextLabel properties, caller Compose animation and control-specific full-value disclosure are the current surface; no compatibility facade or old timing manager remains.

text_reveal: a truncated reveal text publishes reveal facts: policy, flag, natural width
clippedEssential accepts a reveal path as full-value access
rests in the engine ellipsis for the quiet delay: nothing moves at present
after the delay the strip mounts, the source paint yields, and travel advances left
pauses at the end with the tail fully shown, returns, and rests again as the ellipsis
never runs for text that fits, or for truncated text that did not declare it
a re-solve that makes room retires the reveal cleanly
a source that goes HIDDEN mid-flight retires the strip (found live, 2026-08-04)
dismissing the owning surface retires the reveal with it
reduced motion disables travel entirely — and the static plate remains reachable
a reduced-motion flip mid-flight retires the strip on the next tick
at most ONE strip runs: the first declared target in document order wins
a live disclosure plate for the same label outranks the strip: the reveal rests
text_reveal_stream: paints the placeholder until the first character, then the value
never splits a codepoint as the cursor walks past it
holds the prefix when the cursor runs ahead of a value still arriving
lands the whole value under reduced motion
reads through a binding's `use`, so a Text rebinds when the value changes
value_reveal: a sync before the payload exists leaves the hold ALONE
the animator holds the START value before anything reads it
an explicit abandon releases, and cannot be restarted by a later cue
a window already PAST releases instead of holding — the late-arrival path
runs once, and a repeated cue is a no-op
a NEW epoch rearms on the settled state of the last one
with NO animator the fact is stated immediately, never held
text_disclosure: focus entering the containing focusable presents the static full-value plate
pointer hover presents the plate only after the dwell elapses
touch long-press presents the plate immediately
the plate appears identically under reduced motion (nothing about it moves)
a plate never appears for text that is not truncated
a plate never appears for truncated text that did not declare disclose
ticking with nothing engaged never presents a plate
hovering a second disclosed label replaces the first plate rather than stacking
a refresh under a live pointer plate never swaps it for the focused row's
the same label engaged twice keeps one plate rather than remounting it
pointer leave removes the plate
long-press release removes the plate
focus moving off the label removes the plate
a tap anywhere removes the plate
dismissing the surface removes the plate
unmounting the source node removes the plate on the next refresh
a re-solve that makes room for the label removes the plate
the plate is outside every focus order and mounts nothing focusable
the plate paints above its owner and wears the theme's raised surface
the plate is clamped into the safe viewport
the clamp FOLLOWS a live plate — geometry that changes after mount re-places it
a disclose Text gets a zone; ordinary text and controls get none
a pointer world wires hover; a pure-touch world wires long-press instead
the zone's events drive the SAME plates the seams do, end to end
a truncated disclosing Toggle presents its LABEL through the same plate a Text does
an UNdisclosed Toggle stays plate-less — the declaration is the permission
the pointer dwell RE-ASKS at expiry: a re-solve that made room presents nothing
...and a value that changed during the dwell discloses the CURRENT string, not the snapshot
a touch class arriving MID-SESSION retrofits the long-press half onto mounted labels

groupRationales.name: removed-toast-composition-service
groupRationales.rationale: Deleted application/presenter toast scheduler, global layer seam and blueprint presentation options. Compose/Engine own presentation lifetimes; Facet no longer owns a global toast composition service.

native_toast: a toast owns its body: the component runs in the toast and is released with it
refuses a node: the body is a component
toast_layer_seam: every `ctx.<key>` the module reads is declared in `Ctx`
every key `Ctx` declares is one the module actually reads
the one construction site passes exactly the declared set — no more, no less
there is exactly ONE construction site
NEGATIVE CONTROL: each set comparison reports the pair that is out of step
all six scalars the ledger called SHARED are gone from the presenter's code
NEGATIVE CONTROL: the stripper removes comments and keeps code
the presenter's tick body delegates one frame of toast time, and owns none of it
the module writes through NO ctx dep — the cost this extraction did not pay
NEGATIVE CONTROL: the write scan sees each of the three write shapes
the module offers exactly the entry points the presenter uses
the public `ToastOpts` has exactly ONE declaration, and its guard set travels with it
the module requires the presenter NOWHERE — the require is one-way
toast_presentation: content-fit width centers short toasts and caps long wrapping text
ordinary slide transitions keep text out of a CanvasGroup texture
invalid placement and width fail before a toast joins the scheduler
a control beneath a live toast still activates
the toast layer is not a presented surface: it never joins the stack
focus is untouched before, during and after
no toast node is focusable, so no navigation can ever reach one
the toast layer sits above every base screen and below every modal
a bottom-docked strip grows UPWARD from the safe-area inset (review R2-F10)
a base screen presented AFTER a modal still sits below it (bands, not a counter)
400 present/dismiss cycles never push a base screen's displayOrder out of its band
the layer appears with the first toast and retires once the last one has left
a toast retires itself on schedule and says why
an explicit dismiss retires it early with reason `manual`
churning toasts through mount and retire returns the core to baseline
the same toasts appear for the same time; only the transition is instant
under reduced motion a toast is fully painted on its first frame
with motion the same toast starts displaced and transparent, then settles
a bottom-docked toast comes up from its own edge instead
the DEFAULT slide needs no fading-plate exception
a caller's own table is MERGED into, and a caller's own plate passes through
a READABLE transition is merged at the read, and still tracks its signal
toast_schedule: shows up to maxVisible and queues the rest, newest last
a toast times out after its duration and the queue promotes in that frame
durations and read floors are per-toast, not global
the defaults are the ratified numbers
the queue is priority-ordered, FIFO within a priority
a more urgent toast NEVER truncates a showing toast's read floor
preemption takes the WEAKEST showing toast, not the oldest
a queued toast no more urgent than the weakest showing one just waits
a same-key toast replaces its QUEUED predecessor immediately
a same-key toast replaces a SHOWING one only once its floor is met
at the queue cap the LOWEST-priority queued toast is dropped, with a reason
a newcomer that IS the least urgent thing drops itself, and says so
a SHOWING toast is never dropped for capacity
dismiss retires a showing toast and promotes the queue in the same call
dismiss finds a QUEUED toast too, and an unknown id is a false, not an error
clear retires everything, each with its reason

groupRationales.name: removed-theme-inference-and-glyph-shims
groupRationales.rationale: Deleted icon ASCII namespace glyph derivation and custom asset decode/inference/failure-ledger mechanisms. Native ImageLabel content and explicit theme asset data replace them.

icon_ns_glyph: derives the glyph from the name after the namespace
the derived glyph passes the safe-glyph rule
table names keep their curated glyphs (the derivation never shadows them)
a plain unknown name still resolves to nil (schema keeps it a construction error)
a namespace with no letter after the colon resolves to nil, never a broken char
theme_asset_judgement: art entirely outside a ClipsDescendants host is NOT judgeable
art the player can see any pixel of IS judgeable, including a partial row
a one-pixel overlap is enough, and a shared edge is not
EVERY clipping ancestor has to be satisfied, not just the nearest
a clipping host with no area clips everything inside it
an ancestor that does not clip cannot make art unjudgeable
the four earlier faces still answer, and each names itself
the D5 row itself: off-window consumers no longer condemn a shared asset
a deferred judgement is not a verdict of healthy: the same art, scrolled in
the mute is for the HEALTHY siblings; the failed asset's art keeps drawing
...and that art is JUDGEABLE, which is what breaks the deadlock
a recovery clears the slot and un-mutes every sibling, once
NO OSCILLATION: the inferred ledger is a monotone lattice
the authoritative provider is still authoritative
a package swap clears the decode history with the failure ledger

groupRationales.name: removed-primitive-and-host-policy-shims
groupRationales.rationale: Divider was a Facet primitive facade (native Frame/style now); matrix_rows selected old simulator presets and asserted deleted Facet environment distance/size classes; mouse_scroll implemented deleted custom scroller pointer/paging shim (native ScrollingFrame/UIPageLayout now). No old facade is preserved.
